filo export [DIR] -o FILE [--no-scan] [--workers N]
filo export duplicates [DIR] -o FILE [--no-scan] [--workers N]

  Scans first (DIR only; every root for export duplicates), then writes every
  file under DIR (inside a root), or under every root, as CSV (UTF-8) to FILE. A
  root that cannot be scanned stops the export. If FILE exists, filo asks before
  replacing it (only a regular file, and only at a terminal). Columns: id,
  export, directory, name, size, modified, file_date, retention, keep_until,
  tags. Fill in retention in a spreadsheet (a period such as 7y counted from
  file_date, a date, forever, or a policy name: filo help policies) and tags
  (separated by ;, see filo help tag), correct a name to rename the file, or
  change its directory to move it within its root, then run filo update FILE. A
  directory named duplicates is given with ./ before it (./duplicates). A blank
  file_date is filled in from the file name when the name holds one clear date
  (2023-03-14, 20230314, or 2023-03 for the month's last day), marked with !
  (!2023-03-14): check it and remove the ! to accept it; a period on a row whose
  date is still marked is refused. On a large system, export one directory at a
  time.

  export duplicates writes each duplicate group (two or more copies of the same
  content; hard links to one file are one copy) with a copy under DIR, with all
  its copies. Columns: id, export, group, copies, directory, name, size,
  modified, file_date, retention, keep_until, action. In each group you decide
  on, write keep for the copy to keep and delete for the rest (or k and d); keep
  on two or more copies keeps them as separate files, each with its own
  retention; always on every row means the content belongs everywhere. A group
  left blank is left alone. filo delete FILE carries the CSV out.

Flags
  -o FILE                  the CSV to write; an existing file is replaced only
                           after asking
  --no-scan                export the register as it is, without scanning first
  --workers N              for the scan: files hashed in parallel, 1-64 (default
                           4; use 1 on a spinning disk)
